# Which repository files a host RUNS, and which it does not. "Update available" is offered only
# when a file named `runtime` here changes (the owner's rule); a change to `noise` alone is not an
# update. Read by panel/ops/system_ops.py (_update_rules) FROM THE COMMIT BEING OFFERED, so naming a
# new tool's config file here is itself a noise change: no panel is offered it. These lists used to
# live in system_ops.py, and adding .sonarcloud.properties to them (#382) changed a file the panel
# runs, which offered every panel that one line as an update.
#
# A line is `runtime <path>` or `noise <path>`. A path ending in / is a directory, one with * ? or
# [ is a glob over the whole path (case-insensitive), any other is one file. The most specific entry
# decides: a file over a glob over a directory, and a longer directory over a shorter one. A tie
# goes to runtime. A path named by nothing here also counts as runtime, so a host is never left
# behind on a file nobody classified; tests/unit (part03) fails the build for any repository file
# left unnamed, holds every module the panel imports and every file the installers read to
# `runtime`, and every single-file entry to a file that exists.

# ── what a host runs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
runtime panel/
runtime static/
runtime templates/
runtime translations/
# The panel's entry points, the installers and recovery tools (install.sh re-stages recover.sh,
# db_maintenance.py and itself root-owned on every update), the two lockfiles pip installs from,
# and VERSION (the version a checkout without .git reports).
runtime app.py
runtime manage.py
runtime db_maintenance.py
runtime VERSION
runtime install.sh
runtime uninstall.sh
runtime recover.sh
runtime reset-password.sh
runtime requirements.txt
runtime requirements-bootstrap.txt
# Inside tools/, which is otherwise noise.
#
# tools/panel-helper is the root-owned end of the sudo boundary. It lives outside the panel's
# checkout once installed, and only install.sh, run as root, can refresh it; the update badge is
# what tells the operator to do that. Classified as noise, a commit that changed ONLY the helper
# raised no badge and appeared in no changelog, so the panel moved on while the installed helper
# did not: it then answers an unknown verb with rc 2 and no fallback, and the feature behind that
# verb fails silently.
runtime tools/panel-helper
# tools/gamedig: install.sh installs these three root-owned on every host and runs the script, and
# every game account runs the tree it installs. A commit changing only them (every Dependabot bump
# of the lockfile) is an update. privileged.GAMEDIG_FILES names them; a unit test holds the two
# together.
runtime tools/gamedig/package.json
runtime tools/gamedig/package-lock.json
runtime tools/gamedig/install-gamedig.sh

# ── what it does not ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
noise .github/
noise docs/
noise tests/
noise tools/
noise .vscode/
noise .clusterfuzzlite/
noise *.md
noise LICENSE
noise license.*
noise .gitignore
noise .gitattributes
noise .dockerignore
# requirements.in is what requirements.txt is compiled FROM: neither the panel nor install.sh reads
# it. A dependency reaches a host through requirements.txt, which tests/unit holds to lock every
# name in the .in. requirements-bootstrap.in is the same for pip's own lockfile,
# requirements-bootstrap.txt, which install.sh does read, and which therefore counts.
noise requirements.in
noise requirements-bootstrap.in
# Analysis and lint configuration, read by the scanners alone.
noise .codacy.yaml
noise .prospector.yaml
noise .semgrepignore
noise .sonarcloud.properties
noise static/js/.eslintrc.json
# static/vendor's two manifests describe the vendored files to the dependency graph and osv-scanner;
# nothing installs from them and no panel reads them. The files they describe stay runtime (static/).
# Classified runtime, a lockfile-only Dependabot bump would have offered every panel an update.
noise static/vendor/package.json
noise static/vendor/package-lock.json
